sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dry Bulk Marine Transport and Brokerage of Granular Elemental Sulfur

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (Investment Chapter; in force 31 Oct 2012)
Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement (Investment Chapter; in force 1 Apr 2013)
Panama–Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 28 Jul 1984, as amended; currently in force)

Panama DTAAs in force per the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) 'Convenios en vigor' annex, including (without limitation) Barbados, Mexico, UAE, Qatar, Spain and Luxembourg; exhaustive consolidation to be certified from the DGI at diligence date

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended; Articles 1-7 (creation and endowment), 18-22 (council and officers), and 41-44 (registration and public effect)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama – Private Interest Foundations Department)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter / Deed of Incorporation) registered in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Foundation Charter must state an initial endowment, commonly USD 10,000. There is no escrow account requirement; the endowment may consist of cash, securities, or other lawful assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founder's initial endowment to the Private Interest Foundation, as stated in the Foundation Charter, is hereby accepted and recorded in the foundation's asset register. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office address at [Street, Suite, Panama City, Panama] be and is hereby adopted as the foundation's seat and legal domicile for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] be and are hereby appointed as members of the Foundation Council, with [Name] acting as President and [Name] as Secretary, each to serve one-year terms. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute letters of credit, and sign commercial contracts within the objects of the foundation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in Panama (Notaría del Circuito)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panama-licensed notary and execute the Foundation Charter in Spanish. The charter must include the foundation name, registered office address, initial endowment, Foundation Council members, beneficiary provisions, and dissolution rules. The notary will affix the protocol number and deliver the certified original.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of proposed Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, amend the charter and re-execute before the same notary. No governmental query is involved at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Foundation Charter with the Private Interest Foundations Department either in person or through a licensed attorney. Pay the applicable registration fee and obtain the certified inscription certificate evidencing the foundation's legal existence.
required_dossiers: Payment receipt of the registration fee
Power of Attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues an 'observaciones' memorandum requiring corrections, remedy the identified defects within ten business days and re-present the corrected charter with the applicable re-examination fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the DGI after receiving the Public Registry inscription certificate. Submit the required forms to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) and the taxpayer identification number (NIT). If the foundation is not engaged in local taxable activities, obtain a non-resident RUC or exemption certificate as applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation registration certificate from the Public Registry
Passport copies of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the application due to data inconsistencies, correct the information and file an administrative reconsideration or resubmit the complete package before the same office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección General de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RUC, registered address details, and business activity declaration with the Municipality of Panama. Pay the municipal tax rate applicable to commercial brokerage activities and receive the Aviso de Operación, the general operating license for conducting business within Panama.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or title deed for the registered office
Initial balance sheet or capital statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality issues a query or tax assessment, submit supporting financial declarations and pay any corrected municipal fees before the Rentas Municipales office; appeal is available within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Banking AML/KYC and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendency of Banks of Panama (SBP) regulated commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach a licensed Panamanian bank (e.g., Banco General, BAC Internacional, or similar) with the foundation package. Complete the bank's anti-money-laundering customer due diligence form, provide source-of-funds explanations, and execute the account opening agreement for the foundation's commercial treasury operations.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of Foundation Council members
Description of business purpose and expected trade volumes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide additional source-of-wealth evidence such as audited financial statements, trade counterparty contracts, and corporate statements to satisfy the KYC requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección General de Rentas Municipales; Ministry of Environment (MiAMBIENTE) for environmental registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating License) for dry bulk marine transport and brokerage of granular elemental sulfur

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Registration; no full EIA required for pure brokerage or office-based operations unless bulk storage or handling of elemental sulfur exceeds low-threshold quantities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Executive Decree No. 92 of 2013 (pH 6-9, BOD5 < 250 mg/L, TSS < 125 mg/L); air emissions must satisfy National Ambient Air Quality Standards (Executive Decree No. 818 of 1967); elemental sulfur storage requires dust suppression, spill containment, and sulfur-specific fire response measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-Safety Certificate issued by the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC); structural load inspection certificate from a licensed structural engineer for any storage area; workplace safety clearance from the Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) for employee occupational health conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), under the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama; primary portal is the SICE (Sistema Integrado de Consulta Electrónica) at www.dgi.gob.pa, supplemented by the DGI e-tax platform (Tasas y Trámites Digitales) and the Mandatory Electronic Invoicing Portal 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) as follows: (1) Appoint and legally empower a resident representative or agent in Panama; (2) File the foundation deed (Escritura Pública), registered statutes, and FIJA (Ficha Única de Identificación) with supporting apostilled/consularised corporate documents; (3) Submit the online RUC application via SICE, including the notarial certificate of existence and sworn statement of the resident agent; (4) Obtain the provisional RUC and then the definitive RUC once DGI verifies the domicile and legal representative; (5) Simultaneously activate the digital electronic signature (Firma Electrónica) issued through the Autoridad Nacional para la Innovación Gubernamental (AIG); (6) Register for ITBMS and for mandatory electronic invoicing if the PIF undertakes any Panamanian-source commercial activity; the definitive RUC is typically issued within five to ten business days of complete submission.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama operates a strict territorial source-of-income tax system. A Private Interest Foundation created under Law 25 of 1995 is treated as a hybrid entity whose foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian tax net; the PIF is not a pass-through for domestic purposes but is exempt from corporate income tax and ITBMS when it restricts its activities to offshore trade, provided it does not habitually execute commercial acts within Panama or derive income from Panamanian sources. Trading profits on sulfur sold to non-resident buyers and delivered ex-Panama are therefore not Panamanian-source and are outside the taxable base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not adopt US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) election to register the PIF as an ordinary ITBMS taxpayer versus remaining a non-taxpayer entity for offshore-only operations; (ii) election to be taxed under the simplified micro/small-taxpayer regime where qualifying turnover limits apply; (iii) election to treat cross-border service supplies as 0% 'export services' under DGI rules; (iv) election for the transfer-pricing documentation framework for multinational groups; and (v) election by the founder to define the PIF's activities in the foundation charter so as to preserve territorial non-taxation. No hybrid-mismatch matching election exists in domestic law; Panamanian entities are subject to the OECD BEPS-aligned transfer pricing rules and to reporting under the Multilateral Convention for the exchange of information.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's federal value-added tax / sales and services transfer tax), governed by the Código Fiscal and amended by tax-reform legislation in force from 2025.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory de minimis turnover threshold: any person habitually engaged in the transfer of movable goods or the rendering of services in Panama must register for ITBMS, regardless of annual revenue. A simplified regime applies to qualifying micro-entrepreneurs with limited turnover, but such mini-taxpayer status is generally unavailable or inappropriate for international commodity trading entities. A PIF conducting only offshore operations and having no Panamanian-source transactions is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies under the DGI 'Facturación Electrónica de Panamá' framework. Invoices must be transmitted in XML format through the DGI's digital-authorization service (AET – Autorización Electrónica de Facturas) using the taxpayer's digital signature; the system validates the invoice in near real-time, assigns a unique authorization code, and applies digital 'stamping' before the invoice is legally effective between the parties. Taxpayers are required to integrate their ERP or billing systems with the DGI's web services/API, transmit all sales documents electronically, and report the resulting ITBMS obligations through the electronic themise return. Paper invoicing is not permitted for general-regime taxpayers, and failing to obtain prior electronic authorization renders the invoice non-deductible and subject to fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The definitive export of tangible goods from Panamanian customs territory, including dry bulk granular sulfur, is taxable at 0% ITBMS. Eligibility requires: (i) the seller to be a registered ITBMS taxpayer; (ii) the goods to physically leave Panama under a valid customs export declaration; (iii) transport by a duly documented vessel or carrier; (iv) the buyer to be a non-resident party and payment to be received from outside Panama; and (v) possession of the statutory documentation bundle. Services that are rendered to non-residents and effectively consumed abroad are also zero-rated as 'export services' where the economic benefit arises outside Panama. Input VAT attributable to the exported goods may be credited or refunded to the exporter on application to the DGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduana – DUA) duly stamped by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá
Bill of Lading (B/L) or equivalent ocean transport document confirming the cargo destined abroad
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 credit confirmation evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Commercial Invoice and Packing List (or official weight certificate for bulk sulfur cargo)
Independent surveyor's Certificate of Analysis and weight report (e.g., SGS) substantiating quantity and quality
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit procedures systematically cross-match the DUA, port/terminal records, the electronic invoice authorization codes, and the banking remittance evidence. Failure to substantiate the physical departure of the goods or receipt of the foreign currency within the applicable period leads to retrospective revocation of the 0% rate and reassessment at 9% ITBMS on the full sales value, plus default surcharges, statutory monthly interest, and fines for false or incomplete declarations. Where the exporter knowingly simulates exports or uses back-to-back documentation to manufacture a refund, the conduct constitutes tax fraud under Panama's evasion legislation and may trigger criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and confiscation of the underlying goods or proceeds; the DGI may also claw back refunds already paid for the full statutory limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank with monetary sovereignty. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established under Decree-Law No. 9 of 26 February 1998 (General Banking Law), is the sole prudential banking and FX supervisor. Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and quasi-central clearing counterparty, while the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) serves as the financial intelligence unit. No foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control board exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the United States Dollar (USD) is legal tender of unlimited acceptance, and the Balboa exists only as 1:1 token coinage with no electronic market. Both current-account flows (imports, exports, servicing, profit remittances) and capital-account flows (PIF endowment contributions, loans, repatriation) are free of convertibility licensing, central-bank approval, or outflow quotas. Practical barriers are strictly bank-level: AML, CFT, OFAC, and beneficial-owner checks under Law 23 of 2015. Profit remittances from a PIF to foreign beneficiaries are non-Panamanian-source income and are not taxed or restricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Because domestic legal tender is already USD, there is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds, no conversion quota, and no statutory timeline for retaining or repatriating receipts from granular sulfur ore sales. The obligations are administrative: export declarations via the national customs platform (SICE) through a licensed broker; five-year retention of fully documented export dossiers (commercial invoice, bill of lading, LC/MT103, surveyor certificate) under Law 23 of 2015; and Currency Transaction Reports plus unusual-transaction reports to the UAF for cash or flows breaching the USD 10,000 threshold or showing pattern mismatches.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Commercial Letter of Credit line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW for any unlicensed offshore EMI as primary treasury rail. Panama has no passporting regime for EU/UK e-money institutions; Decree-Law 9 of 1998 restricts deposit-taking and payment services to SBP-licensed entities, so a foreign EMI cannot open settlement accounts at Tier-1 Panamanian banks without local licensing. Medium viability exists only as a supplementary collection channel: an authorized overseas EMI may gather small B2B receivables provided funds are re-cleared into the Panamanian operational account within 24 hours and the flow is disclosed at onboarding. For volumes below USD 30 million per annum, reliance exclusively on domestic licensed bank rails is the compliance-optimal design.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Effectively mandatory. SBP-aligned customer due diligence requires positive identification of the founder, foundation council members, protector, and ultimate beneficiaries; all Tier-1 banks demand an in-person interview in Panama City for first-time non-resident PIF clients. The session verifies original passports, executes wet signatures, confirms the foundation charter inscription at the Public Registry, and validates the registered agent's compliance certificate. Remote opening is rarely granted and only for existing bank relationships. A single travel mission combining the bank interview, notary certification of council resolutions, and registered-agent signature is the strongly recommended onboarding path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived use of the PIF as an opaque privacy veil because internal beneficiary registers may remain private and the foundation council can amend beneficiaries subsequently.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified foundation charter with Public Registry inscription number; certified English translation; internal Regulations (Reglamento) detailing the legitimate commodity-trading purpose; sworn beneficial-owner statement naming founder and living beneficiaries; current Transparency Registry filing receipt under Law 23 of 2015; and a legal opinion from the registered agent confirming the absence of bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity on the initial capital injection, as Panamanian law permits endowment with assets without mandatory ex ante proof of origin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized endowment deed stating the exact USD amount; 12 months of founder's bank statements; personal net-worth statement; audited financial statements of the founder; and executed Stage 1-3 sulfur purchase/sale contracts evidencing that the endowment derives from genuine trade receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and counterparty geographic risk in sulfur supply chains, particularly where producers, shipping flags, or end-buyers touch OFAC, UK, EU, or UN-restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction trade compliance file: counterparty registry/UBO certificates; dated negative screening reports against UN, OFAC SDN, EU, UK, and Panamanian lists; commercial contract; master LC or bill of lading; independent weight/quality certificates from SGS, Intertek, or Bureau Veritas; and a bank-accepted counterparty risk-rating sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-pattern mismatch: high-frequency MT103 flows at account opening without an accessible underlying trade-lifecycle dossier, triggering STRs to the UAF and possible account freeze.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-registered trade data room shared with the bank containing PO/contract, LC copy, loading documents, SICE customs entry, invoice, vessel data, and settlement reconciliation. A monthly wire-versus-trade matching register signed by the PIF treasurer is maintained; records are preserved for five years; the registered agent's undertaking to update beneficial-owner data within 30 days of change is lodged in the KYC file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound endowment or shareholder-loan wires are executed via SWIFT MT103 in USD, with the beneficiary styled as the PIF's legal name and the reference clause reciting the foundation charter article governing the endowment. The receiving Panamanian bank places the credit on manual compliance hold until the remitter name is reconciled with the UBO declaration and the notarized endowment deed; release occurs typically within one business day. No SBP approval is required, but amounts exceeding the bank's threshold (commonly USD 10,000) generate a Currency Transaction Record to the UAF. A shareholder loan requires a formal council-resolution and written loan agreement; interest is exposed to Panama's 12.5% withholding only if characterized as Panamanian-source income, so offshore trade-financing loans should be documented as used exclusively outside Panama.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement uses two rails: (i) documentary credit rail by SWIFT MT700 issued by the Panamanian bank in favor of the sulfur supplier against commercial invoice, full-set clean-on-board bill of lading, and third-party inspection certificate; transferable LC mechanisms (MT720/MT710) are used where the PIF acts as middle broker; and (ii) open-account rail via MT103 for freight to vessel owners, port agents, surveyors, and post-shipment settlement of receivables, with MT202 COV for interbank cover when the beneficiary bank demands it. Domestic USD transfers use Panama's local ACH processor (Centro de Procesamiento Interbancario) and are irrelevant to cross-border flows. MT760 standby LCs or demand guarantees are added to secure take-or-pay performance obligations of the PIF's customers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC plain-vanilla FX forwards in EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and CHF/USD under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA, capped at the face value of non-USD receivables and prohibited for speculative positioning
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH and USD/BRL executed via the relationship bank's global markets desk; no SBP or FX-authority pre-approval required given the absence of exchange controls
Cross-currency swaps (USD against EUR or JPY, physically settled) used solely to hedge non-USD vessel charter or refinancing exposure if the PIF later holds marine-asset receivables

Clean FX options (EUR/USD, USD/JPY) with upfront premium, permissible only where the foundation's internal regulations expressly authorize hedging derivatives, each trade backed by a foundation-council resolution and a beneficiary risk acknowledgment

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado (Annual Private Interest Foundation Government Fee)
stage_5.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry) — General Directorate of Revenue (DGI) collection portal
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 (calendar first quarter); no grace period
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge; certificate of good standing withheld; three consecutive years of non-payment may trigger administrative strike-off of the foundation from the Registro Público.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential rate applies to elemental sulfur mineral ore trading. Panama applies territorial taxation, so foreign-source income from extraterritorial freight legs and brokerage services is excluded from taxable income. Tax losses may be carried forward for 5 years; no additional investment allowance or free-zone deduction is available to a Private Interest Foundation without a qualifying SEM/free-zone license.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 020 (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas); filed electronically through the DGI T@P e-filing portal (dgi.mef.gob.pa)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly/quarterly advance tax declarations (Form 020-C) may be required depending on the estimated annual tax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, no later than 31 March of the following year; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months after the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIF must first register with DGI through its resident agent and enter the assigned RUC; no filing is possible without an active RUC.
Use the exact foundation name from the Panama Public Registry and the address of the registered agent; a commercial alias or foreign branch address will delay processing.
Enter the fiscal year actually used. If no different fiscal year was elected at establishment, the period is 1 January – 31 December.

Report all income taxable in Panama, including commissions on sulfur mineral ore brokerage where the negotiation, conclusion or execution is attributable to Panama and vessel loading/unloading occurs in Panamanian ports or territorial waters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross income excluded under territoriality
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare only the non-taxable foreign freight and brokerage portions, ensuring the split follows shipping and INCOTERMS documentation; DGI expects a supporting source-and-contract schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions attributable to Panama-source income (cost of ore, freight, stevedoring, marine insurance, brokerage, bank charges)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach itemized invoices, bills of lading, and SWIFT/LC documents. Deductions must be actual, documented and necessary; related-party payments must satisfy transfer pricing documentation thresholds.
Carry Box 201 minus Box 401, with any adjustment for non-deductible expenses. A nil return is required if the PIF had no Panama-source income.
Multiply Box 601 by 25%. No preferential rate is available to a PIF without a qualifying SEM/free-zone license.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable advance payments and withheld taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim the monthly/quarterly advances already paid during the year and any valid Panama withholding tax credits; attach payment vouchers and receipts from T@P.
Pay the remaining balance by the filing deadline through the T@P portal; refund requests trigger DGI desk audit, so maintain all source documents at the registered office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due (capped at 50%) plus statutory daily interest at the annual 10% rate; formal fines up to USD 5,000 apply for non-submission, RUC suspension may be ordered, and fraudulent returns trigger criminal tax evasion sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid out of Panama-source profits; the paying entity must withhold and remit the 5% to DGI, and the shareholder bears no further Panamanian tax on the dividend. Dividends wholly sourced from foreign-source profits are outside territorial withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claims under an applicable double tax treaty require submission to the DGI before payment: (1) a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's home tax administration; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration covering the dividend, interest or royalty; and (3) the relevant DTA application form. Only after DGI validation may the withholding agent apply the reduced treaty rate; the approved set must be kept in the payer's books for 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory effective withholding for royalties and interest paid to non-residents is generally 12.5% (25% applied to the 50% treated as Panama-source), subject to any lower DTA rate under Panama's limited treaty network and to TRC/beneficial ownership compliance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: annual related-party transactions equal to or exceeding USD 1,500,000 (B/.1,500,000 at parity); Master File: multinational group consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding USD 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report: group consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding USD 750,000,000.
